summary: Swift Point (Green Head) Light on the Saint John River: lit 1869, rebuilt 1896, burned in June 2017 and replaced by the Coast Guard in 2018.

light.note: Coast Guard list gives Fl G 4s, focal height 28.1 m, range 5 nm; LighthouseFriends gives a nominal range of 4 miles.

structures.note: first light at Swift Point, shown from a mast; replaced 1896 (LighthouseFriends)
white square wooden building 50 ft high with dioptric apparatus, contract $579; burned 13 June 2017
built in Saint John and carried to the site; PVC and vinyl cladding; Coast Guard list gives 13.9 m

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Walk of about a kilometre through the woods from the main road (Global News).

events.note: Saint John River lights placed in operation 20 August 1869
lantern caught fire; light suspended for a few nights (LighthouseFriends; repeated by the Canadian Press)
new square wooden tower 24 ft east of the old mast light; contract G. W. Palmer, $579 (quoted from the 1896 Marine report via LighthouseFriends)
seventh-order dioptric lens replaced the pressed lens
mechanical fog bell installed by day labour at $206, replacing the hand foghorn
fire reported around 10 p.m. Tuesday 13 June 2017; almost completely destroyed; cause not determined
Coast Guard rebuilt the tower; foundation poured November 2017; in operation about mid-January 2018

corrections.proposed: light on a mast (1869); square wooden tower (1896, burned 2017); square pyramidal tower (2018, 13.9 m, standing)
corrections.why: LighthouseFriends describes the 1869 light as shown from a mast and the tower as built in 1896; the present tower dates from 2018.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1869 light was on a mast; the first tower dates from 1896 and was burned in 2017; the present tower dates from 2018. The 'first year' disagreement is the 1869 mast light against the 1896 tower.
LighthouseFriends gives 13 June 2017; the Canadian Press story, dated 14 June, says the fire was reported around 10 p.m. on Tuesday, which was 13 June. Wikipedia's 14 June is not relied on.

LighthouseFriends says the 2018 tower was built in Saint John and carried to the site; the Coast Guard's account to CHSJ says its aluminum frames were built in Nova Scotia, delivered to Saint John, and installed on site. The story states both and does not choose between them.
LighthouseFriends says Williams served eighteen years before resigning in 1886; its own dates (from 1869) give seventeen. The story gives both the claim and the arithmetic.

notes_for_editor: Fact-checked 2026-10-28. The Looney entry (Greenhead, St. John River, on the 1902-03 Marine keepers' list) was checked against the page image: scan p. 228 is printed p. 215 (New Brunswick, continued), and the Looney row sits on the same line as Greenhead, St. John River, with appointment 14 Oct 1886. The story now cites printed p. 215 with scan p. 228. The 1896 tower is known only from LighthouseFriends's quotation of the 1896 Marine report (not in the local corpus; second-hand, and the story says so). Sources disagree on the range (4 miles nominal on LighthouseFriends, 5 nm on the Coast Guard list); the story does not give a range. The Coast Guard list marks the light seasonal; the story says so. No lost light or wreck is recorded at the station in the sources read. The 1872 fire comes from LighthouseFriends alone (the Canadian Press story repeats it, but the story does not use that). Wikipedia's 1889 date for Williams's resignation and its 14 June date for the fire are not used.
